content.text: I reviewed the file — it's well-built overall, but there's a real accessibility bug: when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, the CSS unconditionally forces `animation-play-state: paused` on the animated elements, with no way for the JS pause/resume toggle to ever override it. So a reduced-motion user who clicks "Resume" sees the button flip state but the animation never actually plays. Let me fix that while keeping the flash-prevention behavior.

content.text: Fixed the reduced-motion bug: previously, users with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` could never actually resume the animation via the pause button — the CSS media query forced `animation-play-state: paused` unconditionally, regardless of JS state. Now the forced pause only applies until JS is ready (`body.js-ready`), after which control fully defers to `body.paused`, so the resume button genuinely works while still avoiding the initial flash of motion.
